_about: What the port draws for what no level pictures - the portals a shot opens, the shot,
the player, and chapter 1's boss with its spikes - as the original's own entities draw
them. Their images are read from the extracted APK beside the remake and never
Each carries its .ent's <EmissiveColor>, because the original dims every sprite it draws
to min(1, ambient + emissive) of its colour (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117), these as much
And each carries its .ent's lighting facts (step 49, the lighting design's G5): static and
applyLight, which decide which 2D lights reach it (Lighting::ReceiverMask); its <Normal>, a
file under the original's entities/normalmaps/, when it names one; and its <Light>, when it
has one, with the z the light's height is measured from.

_source: A LEVEL PROPERTY rather than an entity. Game's level-properties reader does
CheckCustomData('darkest') and, when it is set, SetAmbientLight(DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT)
- and that single call is the whole of what the flag does in that function.
_moved: The ambient light itself, (0.01, 0.01, 0.01), now lives in lighting.json as
darkest_ambient, where the port's lighting reads it (step 45). The flag is carried on
Game::Level, and the layer multiplies every level sprite by min(1, ambient + emissive)
with that ambient in place of the file's.
Its ONE decoded gameplay consequence is not drawing at all:
canSeeAnything = GetAmbientLight() != DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT, so a minion in a darkest
level is BLIND. minions.json records minion sight as not built. Lighting::Ambient is the
number sight must compare when it lands.

portal._emissive: portal.ent's <EmissiveColor r=1 g=1 b=1>: min(1, ambient + 1) is 1, so it is never dimmed
portal._lighting: portal.ent: <Entity static=0 applyLight=0>, no <Normal>, no <Light>. Takes no light and gives none

haloSize=50> with <Position x=0 y=0 z=-12>, <Color r=0.6 g=0.6 b=1>, <HaloBitmap>halo.bmp</HaloBitmap>
(the remake's data_inventory.md, 'projectile.ent'). It has no <Scale>, so the light's offset and
range and the halo's size are the file's own (ETHEntityRenderingManager.cpp:180-181,
ETHRenderEntity.cpp:378-385). A live light: it reaches every sprite that applies light, static

script's AddEntity position for projectile.ent is not decoded. 0 is the port's own placement
of the shot, drawn in the player's slot among the art: the player is added at z 0.
How fast the six frames play. The original keeps a _projectileFrameTimer, whose

_source: the original's light_from_projectile.ent, which ETHCallback_light_off adds when a shot lights a torch
(torch.json): Sprite torch_small.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut 1 x 1, PivotAdjust (0, -16), one
ParticleSystem of 12 fire.png particles. Since step 55 (the lighting design's G6) only its light and
halo are drawn: its sprite and its flame are not built (torch.json's _not_built).
_lighting: <Light active=1 static=1 range=512 haloBrightness=0.7 haloSize=300> with <Position x=0 y=-12 z=24>,
<Color r=1 g=0.5 b=0.2>, <HaloBitmap>halo.bmp</HaloBitmap>. A STATIC light: in a level that has
not baked at run time it would reach no static sprite, but lighting the torch is what makes the
level bake at run time (Lighting::RuntimeBake), so it reaches every sprite that applies light. Its
halo is scaled by the live share of its 12 particles, which the port does not build: drawn at 1.

_note: The depth its light's height is measured from. The callback's AddEntity position is not decoded
(the bytecode listing was not at hand for step 55); the layer adds it at the torch's own eth_z,
and this value stands only where a torch has none.

character._source: the original's dark_mage.ent: Sprite magic_portals_hd.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut 4 x 4, PivotAdjust (0, 2); its startFrame 4 is never shown (_initial_direction)
character._emissive: dark_mage.ent's <EmissiveColor r=1 g=1 b=1>: never dimmed by the ambient (what script sets over it is the lighting design's section 5.8, not built)
_lighting: static, so every light reaches it, a static torch's included (ETHEntitySpriteRenderer.cpp:70),
which the remake's fit measured on the original walking past 1-1's torch (fit.md 7.1). Its
lighting height is the level's player marker's eth_z, not a number here.
_initial_direction: (bytes 119493..119839) instructions 39-41 set direction = 2, MOVING_RIGHT. The row a character
stands on IS its direction: SideScrollerCharacter::updateFrame (bytes 130241..130614) instructions
88-102, every update with no walk, SetFrame(idleColumn, findFinalDirection(direction)), which is
row 2 column 0, frame 8, facing right. dark_mage.ent's startFrame 4 is not what shows:
replaced by the first update, and Ethanon's .ent reader has no startFrame read at all
(ETHEntityProperties.cpp reads type, static, shape, blendMode at :228-236; the clone names
startFrame only in its editor). MEASURED: the original stands on frame 8 in all 54 lit levels
where the player is located (the remake's visuals/briefs/systems_3_4.md 3a).

_note: Which row of the sheet walks which way: derived, not testimony. The original's
DIRECTION enum decodes to MOVING_DOWN 0, MOVING_LEFT 1, MOVING_RIGHT 2, MOVING_UP 3
(the remake's tools/asbc), and Ethanon's own sample picks a character's row by its
direction and its column by a frame timer (Sample-project/main.angelscript:102). The
sheet's row 1 faces left and row 2 right. The owner confirmed on 11 September that the
character turns as it walks; not which rows do it. DECODED since: updateFrame calls
SetFrame(column, findFinalDirection(direction)), and no FlipX or SetFlipX is called anywhere
in the bytecode, so walking left is row 1 unflipped. Rows 0 and 3, arm out, are the pushing
rows (findFinalDirection, bytes 131207..131341): push.

_source: DECODED (the remake's out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce). THE ROW:
SideScrollerCharacter::findFinalDirection (bytes 131207..131341) instructions 3-19 return
`pushing ? (direction == 1 ? 0 : 3) : direction` (the 1, MOVING_LEFT, is the CMPIu immediate
read as its vK operand, INFERRED as every such immediate is): pushing left draws row 0, pushing
any other way row 3 (the sheet's rows 0 and 3 hold the arm out left and right). Walking or
standing alike: updateFrame (bytes 130241..130614) passes it the direction at 63-67 and 89-93.
THE LAG: SideScrollerCharacter::update (bytes 153242..153396) calls updateFrame (instruction
18) BEFORE applyForces (29), which calls detectPushing (applyForces, bytes 129676..130142,
instruction 96): an update draws the push the update before found, so the first update
against a wall draws the walk and the update a walk stops on still draws the push.
THE RAY: detectPushing (bytes 130614..131207): when dirVec.x == 0, pushing = false (3-6,
108-111); else a ray from getPosXY() to getPosXY() + normalize(dirVec) x 0.6 x getSize().x +
vector2(0, scale(-6)) (8-52; the arguments pushed last-first put the -6 on y, 6 above, and
scale() makes it 6 level units, not screen pixels), and pushing = GetClosestContact(from, to,
point, normal, 'dark_mage.ent') != null (59-106). getSize() is ETHEntity::GetSize, the
sprite's frame size times the entity's scale (ETHSpriteEntity::GetCurrentSize,
ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652-682): 0.6 x 40 = 24 units at the player's getScale(). dirVec is the
velocity applyForces has just set (instructions 38-56 and 86-91): x = moveVec.x x speedScale,
the walk, y = the body's vertical velocity; and where isTouchingGround is not set (63-84),
x = the body's own x velocity x min(1, GetFPSRate() / 60 x 0.86), 0.86 at the port's fixed
60 Hz tick (air_velocity_share). GetClosestContact(a, b, point, normal, ignore)
(ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:251-268) ignores entities by name alone (ETHEntityNameArrayChooser,
ETHEntityChooser.cpp:49-63) and keeps every other fixture the ray reports
(ETHRayCastCallback.cpp:40-51), sensors included: Box2D's world ray cast has no sensor test
(b2World.cpp:978-995) and a sensor entity has fixtures (ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:109). A
fixture the ray starts inside is not reported (b2PolygonShape.cpp:189-258, b2CircleShape.cpp:
47-82). NEVER WHERE GRAVITY IS OFF: MainCharacter::MainCharacter (bytes 126650..127790)
instructions 10-17 and 35 pass noGravity as SideScrollerCharacter's forceNoImpulse, whose
constructor (bytes 152667..153096) sets pushing = false (73-75) and keeps the flag (77-78),
and update skips applyForces while it is set (20-29): pushing never changes there.
MEASURED: no clip was taken for it (plan F11), but footage F9's take r6 (3-18) holds the right
pad into the corridor wall and draws row 3 at the wall and row 2 after the release, and F13's
fall (1-06, pad held) draws row 2 on every frame of the fall (planning doc step 64).
DECODED: SideScrollerCharacter::SideScrollerCharacter instructions 9-11 set frameStride = 90
(ms), and instructions 80-82 idleColumn = 0. updateFrame instructions 63-86, every update
with a walk, SetFrame(timer.set(0, 3, frameStride, true), findFinalDirection(direction)); with
none (88-102), SetFrame(idleColumn, ...) and the timer is not called. FrameTimer::set (bytes
23254..23650) adds the frame's elapsed ms (instructions 6-11), resets to `first` with no time
only when first or last differ from the last call's (13-44; the first walk's, against the
constructor's 0 and 0, bytes 22535..22652), else steps ONE column once the time reaches the
stride and takes the stride off (45-76). first and last are always 0 and 3, so the column
and its time carry across a stop and a turn, and on a level with gravity a stop adds no time.
Not called while paused or finished: MainCharacter::update (bytes 128578..128850) 6-21. The
loading screen's character keeps the same 90 ms (ui.json character.stride_ms). On the 18
no_gravity levels the same timer also turns while the player stands: no_gravity_motion.
MEASURED: 0.369 s a cycle of four, 92 ms a column, over 7 cycles of rec11 walking right
(the remake's specs/visuals/scripted.md section 1.4).

_source: DECODED: on a no_gravity level MainCharacter::update (bytes 128578..128850) calls
MainCharacter::linearMotion (bytes 132139..132833) after SideScrollerCharacter::update
(instructions 57, 66), on every update that is neither paused nor finished (6-21).
COLUMN: linearMotion instructions 163-174 call the character's FrameTimer as
set(0, 3, 280, true) and write the column into idleColumn, walking or not. FrameTimer::set
(bytes 23254..23650): the last frame's elapsed ms added (6-11); a reset to `first` with no time
when first or last differ from the last call's (13-44), so the first update resets it against
the constructor's 0 and 0; else one column once the time reaches the stride, the stride taken
off (45-76). updateFrame, which runs first, stands the player on idleColumn (88-102): the column
an update draws is the one the update before left. A walking update also calls set(0, 3, 90,
true) (63-86) and draws that, so it adds its time to the timer twice.
HOVER: linearMotion instructions 8-57, on the first call, set linearMotionAngle = PI + PIb
(hover_start_radians) and keep the pivot as originalPivotAdjust; 59-78 add unitsPerSecond(3), 3 rad
a second of frame time (STimeManager::unitsPerSecond, bytes 8045..8162, min(200, elapsed ms)
/ 1000 x the time factor); 92-112 take PI * 2 off once past it (hover_wrap_radians); 114-161
SetPivotAdjust(originalPivotAdjust + vector2(0, cos(angle) * 1.2)). GetPivotAdjust returns the
stored pivot times the entity's scale and SetPivotAdjust divides by it (ETHEntity.cpp:1019-1026),
and the draw multiplies by it again (ETHEntity.cpp:296): the 1.2 is added in SCREEN pixels, not
scaled with the level (the player is added at getScale(), GameCharacter::GameCharacter
instructions 10-24, screen height / 256). A larger pivot y draws the image higher (the origin
moves down it). A period of 2 PI / 3 = 2.094 s. The port's tick is a fixed 1/60 s, below the
200 ms cap.
PORT DECISION (P2 pattern, as ui.json's credits strip): 1.2 screen px is 0.4267 units only on a
720 px screen (1.2 x 256 / 720), so the port adds hover_screen_px x 256 / hover_at_screen_px
units at every window. R12 fixes the texture tier only. The original's is 1.2 x 256 / the
screen's height (0.64 units at 480 px, 0.28 at 1080 px): left for the owner (planning step 63).
The original's beholder.ent: Sprite beholder.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut 2 x 1. Frame
0 has its eye open and frame 1 shut: ETHCallback_beholder sets 1 while it throws rocks
and 0 otherwise. Its CustomData scale, 0.75, is applied when it appears and replaced
on its first turn: bounce() (utilEntityEffect.angelscript) calls SetScale, which sets
the scale outright (ETHEntity.cpp:601). So it is drawn at its frame's size times its
pulse. The pulse goes from one scale to the other and back by smoothEnd, each way a
stride. While it throws rocks it keeps the last. Its colour is (1, hp / 2, hp / 2).
The original's beholder_spike.ent: Sprite beholder_spike.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut
1 x 1, PivotAdjust (0, 10). Its image points down, and projectileBehaviour turns it to
where it flies: SetAngle(radianToDegree(getAngle(direction))).
A PLACED entity the level pictures, but drawn as its script redraws it: ETHCallback_portal_static
(Portal.angelscript, bytecode bytes 360571..361404, the remake's out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt).
Once, guarded by the uint 'scaled' (ops 1-12, JNZ -> 80 once it is set, ops 17-29 set it):
ops 14-16  thisEntity.Scale(0.8f). ETHEntity::Scale(float) scales the entity AND every particle
system it carries (ETHEntity.cpp:591-599 -> ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:512-518 ->
ETHParticleManager.cpp:444-451, ETHParticleSystem.cpp:27-40, PARTICLE::Scale
ETHParticleManager.h:160-164). The picture is drawn at its frame size times the
scale (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652-682): portal_halo.png 64 -> 51.2 u, the rings 110 -> 88.
ops 31-79  SetColor(GetString('color') == 'red' ? vector3(1, 0.3, 0.3) : vector3(0.3, 0.3, 1)).
An AngelScript call pushes its last argument first (the order systems_3_4 read
_portalColorA by, which footage confirmed), so ops 57-59 push z 0.3, y 0.3, x 1: red.
0.3f is PshC4 1050253722 (0x3E99999A). SetColor writes m_v4Color (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498),
which multiplies the SPRITE's min(1, ambient + emissive) (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117);
a particle is drawn in its own colour times ambient alone (ETHParticleManager.cpp:381-389),
so the rings and the iris are not tinted.
A static entity with a callback runs it on every frame its bucket is drawn
(ETHScene.cpp:572 and 488, ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp:70-74, 90-93 and 145-166), after its particles update.
Footage agrees on the order: red portals read pinker, R/B 0.82 against blue's 0.52 (scripted.md 2.3).
static_portal._not_applied: Scale also scales the entity's collision box (m_controller->Scale). The port's static portal is entered by its trigger_size box, which is gameplay, and is left as it was.

_source: The ring the levels place round a no-portal field, redrawn every frame by its own callback:
ETHCallback_antiportal (AntiPortalManager.angelscript, bytecode bytes 335020..335206, the remake's
out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0). A callback is named for the
entity less its .ent (ETHASUtil.cpp:63-67), so both spellings of the 71 placements run it:
ins 1-25   blinkColor(thisEntity, _portalColorA, _portalColorB, 300). A call pushes its last argument
first, so ins 1 pushes the stride 300, ins 4-8 copy _portalColorB and ins 12-16 _portalColorA.
ins 27-34  AddToAngle(g_timeManager.unitsPerSecond(10f)); ins 27 PshC4 1092616192 is 10f.
_portalColorA and _portalColorB are that file's own globals (initialisers at bytes 306547..306598 and
306617..306668). Each pushes 0f, 0f and then 0.2f (PshC4 1045220557) or 0.4f (1053609165) into vector3,
and a call pushes last-first, so they are vector3(0.2, 0, 0) and vector3(0.4, 0, 0): red. They are the
ANTIPORTAL's colours; a static portal's are static_portal's above, from another callback.
blinkColor(entity, colorA, colorB, stride), utilEntityEffect.angelscript bytes 326140..326616:
ins 1-25   the uint 'blinkElapsedTime' is set to 0 when the entity has none yet: the first call
ins 26-41  AddToUInt('blinkElapsedTime', g_timeManager.getLastFrameElapsedTime())
ins 43-53  elapsedTime = GetUInt('blinkElapsedTime')
ins 55-61  invert = (elapsedTime / stride) % 2 == 1 (DIVu, MODu 2, CMPIu v1, TZ)
ins 63-67  bias = float(elapsedTime % stride) / float(stride)
ins 69-75  bias = invert ? 1 - bias : bias
ins 77-90  SetColor(interpolate(colorA, colorB, bias)), where interpolate(a, b, t) = a + (b - a) x t
(Interpolator.angelscript bytes 314616..314759)
So the red is a TRIANGLE: 0.2 at 0 ms, 0.4 at 300, 0.2 at 600. A period is two strides.
THE TWO CLOCKS ARE NOT THE SAME ONE. blinkColor adds g_timeManager.getLastFrameElapsedTime()
(STimeManager.angelscript bytes 7894..7961), which is uint(float(GetLastFrameElapsedTime()) x
m_factor): ins 3 the engine call, ins 5 uTOf, ins 8 MULf m_factor, ins 9 fTOu. It is NOT capped at 200;
unitsPerSecond (bytes 8045..8162, ins 3-18) is speed x min(200, frame ms) / 1000 x m_factor, which is
(ins 5 pushes the 200, ins 9 calls min; motions.json's linear_motion.frame_cap_ms, the one the port
keeps). Both are capped at 1000 ms by the loop itself (Min(1000.0f, ComputeElapsedTimeF(video)),
android/main.cpp:180-181). m_factor is 1 and pause() sets it to 0, so both stand still under a pause,
and they part company only on a frame longer than 200 ms.
AND THAT CLOCK IS A FLOOR OF EACH FRAME'S MILLISECONDS, SUMMED AS A uint - which the port does NOT
reproduce. The Android loop measures a frame as a float of milliseconds (ComputeElapsedTimeF, gs2d
Application.cpp:36-50, off clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC): AndroidGLES2Video.cpp:66-69, so the fraction
is real and not a timer's quantum) and ETHEngine::Update stores static_cast<unsigned long> of it
(ETHEngine.cpp:147). THE SHIPPED LIBRARY DOES EXACTLY THAT: in libApplication.so
gs2d::ETHEngine::Update(float) at 0xb4100 calls ETHDrawableManager::RemoveTheDead (+0x0e), then
__aeabi_f2uiz at 0x1cb364 (+0x14) and ETHScriptWrapper::SetLastFrameElapsedTime(unsigned long) at
0xf2038 (+0x18). The C++ scene keeps the float (ETHEngine.cpp:166); what the SCRIPT reads is that
truncated uint (uint GetLastFrameElapsedTime(), ETHScriptWrapper.generic.cpp:323,
ETHScriptWrapper.System.cpp:100-107), and blinkColor sums it into the entity's own uint
blinkElapsedTime. So at a steady 60 Hz the original's blink clock gains 16 ms a frame, not 16.667, and
a 600 ms triangle takes 625 ms of wall clock; the script's second truncation (ins 9 fTOu) changes
nothing while m_factor is 1, since uint(16 x 1.0f) is 16. unitsPerSecond reads the same integer, so the
TURN is slow by the same factor. The port's clock is its own tick (kTick, 1/60 as a float), so the
port's blink and turn run 16.667/16 = 4.17 % fast of the original's at 60 Hz and reach opposite phase
after 450 ticks (7.5 s). NOT emulated here: this is the one clock every scripted motion reads, so
flooring it is a port-wide change and its own step (the record's step 72, WHAT THIS STEP DOES NOT DO).
WHAT IS DRAWN. SetColor writes m_v4Color's rgb and keeps its alpha (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498), and the sprite
is drawn at min(1, ambient + emissive) x m_v4Color (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117). All 71 placements carry
emissive (1, 1, 1) (antiportal.ent's EmissiveColor), so that term is 1 on every level, chapter 4's dark
ones too, and the ring is drawn at the blink's own colour, added (antiportal.ent blendMode 1). No placement
carries an eth_color, so writing the rgb and multiplying it in are the same here; the port writes it.
AddToAngle adds to m_angle (ETHEntity.cpp:444-447, ETHEntityController.cpp:145-148), which the draw turns
the picture by (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:105, :122), counter-clockwise on the screen; the converter wrote each
node's angle negated (tscn.py:432-433).
antiportal.ent is static=1, so the original runs this callback only while the ring's bucket is on screen
(00_order 8.12c): it starts a ring's blink and its turn from the frame it is first seen. The port runs
every one from the level's first tick, as it runs motions.json's placed pictures (a recorded divergence).
The phase the original starts at also rests on the INFERRED immediate 1 in ins 58; no still can show it.
_measured: systems_3_4 4b (work_s34/antiportal_census.py) over 105 library frames of the 20 rings whose camera the
port's own ring confirms: the colour factor c_R median 0.218, p90 0.322 and max 0.396, against the
decoded ceiling of 0.400; c_G median 0.017 (p90 0.050) and c_B 0.000. 8 of those 20 rings reach 0.35 or
more, so the red is not scaled down. The low median is unexplained and is not the port's to fit: the
library holds a few fixed delays into each level, so its phases are not uniform, and a ring sits behind
the level's art at eth_z -4 to -16. The gate is the port's own time series (00_order section 7, 4.2).
white_ring.png is symmetric about its centre to 1 % (the brief's hd rim angular s.d. 2.3 on a mean of
242), so the turn moves almost no pixel: it is pinned by test_mp_layer, not by a capture.
TWO GATE ROWS ARE RECORDED DEVIATIONS, not properties of this data: 1-07 antiportal_687 reads low
because the PORT draws that ring behind art the original draws it in front of (a draw order, open), and
4-07 antiportal_2166 because art BOTH builds draw covers it (its eth_z -12). The record's step 72,
RECORDED DEVIATIONS, carries both with their measurements.

_source: The dial the original adds behind every timed crystal (35 in 20 levels: every inline crystal with a
uint `time`). The original's timer.ent: Sprite timer.png (128 x 64, no hd or fullhd twin), SpriteCut
4 x 2, blendMode 0, static 0, applyLight 0, PivotAdjust (0, 0), Scale 1, no <Light>, no particles.
Cell 0 shows eight wedges and cell 7 one. The script is in the remake's out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt
(md5 48fe65ce...), ETHCallback_crystal.angelscript:
addTimerToCrystal, bytes 424766..425217, called by ETHCallback_crystal when `time` is set:
ins 2-5     g_scale.getScale(), the scale AddEntity gives it: 1 in the port's units
ins 12-25   crystal.GetPosition() - vector3(0, 0, 2): a call pushes its last argument first, so
the 2f of ins 13 is z. The dial stands 2 BEHIND the crystal
ins 29-36   AddEntity('timer.ent', that, the scale)
ins 50-96   its uint `time` the crystal's, `elapsedTime` 0, `crystalID` the crystal's id
ins 100-102 SetAlpha(0.5f)
ETHCallback_timer, bytes 425217..426274, every frame:
ins 1-13    elapsedTime += the frame's milliseconds, which is the SAME clock the antiportal's
blink reads: g_timeManager.getLastFrameElapsedTime(), a uint of FLOORED frame
milliseconds (antiportal's _source above). A port-wide note, not this entry's to fix.
ins 53-100  the crystal by its id: gone (taken), elapsedTime += time, which is expiry; there,
SetPositionXY(crystal.GetPositionXY()) - it follows the crystal. The frame it finds
the crystal gone still compares the copy of elapsedTime ins 24-27 took, so it runs
ins 204-252 once more where the dial stood, and the x 0.9 starts on the next frame
ins 102-103 CMPu elapsedTime, time; JNP: while elapsed <= time, ins 204-252; after, ins 105-199
ins 204-231 bounce(this, V2_ONE, vector2(1.15, 1.15), max(400, time - elapsed))
ins 233-252 SetFrame(min(max(int(float(elapsed) / float(time) * 8f), 0), 7))
ins 105-125 SetScale(GetScale() * 0.9f); SetAlpha(GetAlpha() * 0.9f)
ins 127-182 while the crystal is there: AddScaledEntity('crystal_vanish.ent', its position +
(0, 0, scale(20)), scale(1.3)), playCrystalVanishSound, DeleteEntity(crystal). The
crystal goes at its time, with a burst. NOT BUILT HERE: the burst is the visuals plan's
step 10.2, and the sim's crystal already goes (Goals::Crystal::expired)
ins 184-199 GetScale().x < 0.1f: DeleteEntity(this). GetScale is the entity's own scale, which
bounce set as pulse x m_scaleFactor (below), not the pulse: see screen_px_per_unit
bounce, utilEntityEffect.angelscript bytes 327057..327527: blinkElapsedTime from 0, taking the same
frame times (ins 1-39); invert = (elapsed / stride) % 2 == 1 in uints (ins 55-61); bias =
float(elapsed % stride) / float(stride), 1 - bias when inverted (ins 63-75); SetScale(interpolate(

_screen_px_per_unit: SGlobalScale.m_scaleFactor, which the dial's scale is stored in. bounce (utilEntityEffect.angelscript bytes
327057..327527) ins 90-102 is SetScale(g_scale.scale(the pulse)), and the vector2 SGlobalScale::scale
(bytes 5878..5975) ins 3-8 multiplies by m_scaleFactor; ETHEntity::GetScale returns what SetScale stored
(Ethanon ETHEntity.cpp:601-613). bounce runs on every live frame, the last included (ins 102-103 -> 204-231),
so the shrink starts from pulse x m_scaleFactor whatever AddEntity was given. m_scaleFactor is
m_absoluteSize 256 from main on (00_order 8.12a; view.json's height_px). The screen is 720 px tall by the
owner's standing ruling R12, the fixed 720 selection (as ui.json's speed_at_screen_px), so 720 / 256. The
original's own dial therefore lasted longer on a taller screen; the port takes the 720 one. The port draws
the dial at the pulse in its own units (the cell x scale): only the deletion test takes this factor
